items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 14.9 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: When you had dinner at 8 pm or later, which was 63.6% of the time, your sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more than after earlier dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar rose 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 9.4 hours of overnight fasting, with 33.3% of nights reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone, although it's not clear how this relates to your sugar.
